# Sample WaferLens reports

Generated from real WM-811K test wafers. Pattern and confidence come from the CNN; text is written by the LLM using only the retrieved knowledge-base notes.

## Confident defect
*Test wafer #0 | true label: Center | generated by: llm*

**Pattern detected:** Center (98% confidence)

**What this usually means:**
- This pattern is often associated with irregular RF operation or unusual liquid flow during processing [S1].
- It is commonly linked to dispense and spin dynamics, or to effects occurring at the centre of a process chamber [S2].
- It may point to processes that act directly on a spinning or centre-fed wafer [S2].

**Suggested checks:**
- Inspecting the coat and develop modules is commonly recommended as a first check [S2].
- Confirming suspicions against the processing history of the tools the wafer passed through [S2].
- Checking whether the pattern repeats across several wafers or lots, as observing multiple maps helps confirm the cause [S2].

**Sources:**
- [S1] Yeonhong Kim, Jonghyeok Im, Monu Nath Baitha, Kyoungsik Kim (2026). Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00961
- [S2] Averroes (2026). Wafer Defect Map Analysis: How to Read Spatial Patterns and Find Root Causes. https://averroes.ai/blog/wafer-defect-map-analysis

## Uncertain prediction
*Test wafer #4 | true label: Edge-Loc | generated by: llm*

**Pattern detected:** Edge-Loc (69% confidence), uncertain; possibly Edge-Ring (15%)

**What this usually means:**
- Edge-Loc is often associated with irregular temperature during annealing, impurities from a load-lock valve [S1], handling contact, or a local fault at the wafer edge [S2].
- Edge-Ring is commonly linked to abnormal temperature

**Sources:**
- [S1] Yeonhong Kim, Jonghyeok Im, Monu Nath Baitha, Kyoungsik Kim (2026). Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00961
- [S2] Averroes (2026). Wafer Defect Map Analysis: How to Read Spatial Patterns and Find Root Causes. https://averroes.ai/blog/wafer-defect-map-analysis

## No defect pattern
*Test wafer #6 | true label: none | generated by: llm*

**Pattern detected:** none (98% confidence)

**What this usually means:**
* Scattered background failures on these wafers are commonly linked to particles and the general process environment [S1][S2].
* A targeted investigation is usually not needed for a single wafer, though monitoring the background failure rate over time may help detect a gradual problem before a clear pattern emerges [S2].

**Sources:**
- [S1] Moo Hyun Kim, Tae Seon Kim (2024). Development of a Wafer Defect Pattern Classifier Using Polar Coordinate System Transformed Inputs and Convolutional Neural Networks. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics13071360
- [S2] Averroes (2026). Wafer Defect Map Analysis: How to Read Spatial Patterns and Find Root Causes. https://averroes.ai/blog/wafer-defect-map-analysis
